figures.caption: Table 1: Inter-rater reliability within human experts and LLM judges (Gemini-3.1-Pro, Claude-Opus-4.6, GPT-5.2). Here, n denotes the number of individual judgments, where each judgment is a full evaluation over all cases by one expert or one model run. The best values are highlighted in bold.
Table 2: Alignment between LLM judges and human expert evaluations (21 cases, 65 ratings).

Fig. 3: Overview of the SciVisAgentBench execution and evaluation pipeline. LLM-based SciVis agents interact with SciVis tools and datasets to perform benchmark tasks and produce recorded outcomes. These outcomes are evaluated against ground-truth references using a combination of MLLM judges and deterministic evaluators, yielding visualization quality, efficiency, and final benchmark scores for recorded outcomes.

Table 4: Benchmark performance across all five task suites of SciVisAgentBench using Claude-Opus-4.6 as the LLM judge for evaluation. For each agent+model setting, we report overall score, completion rate, pass@{1,2,3} (i.e., success in at least one of the first k trials), and passˆ{1,2,3} (i.e., success in all k trials). Scores and completion rates are reported as mean±std across three repeated trials.

Table 6: Token usage across all five task suites of SciVisAgentBench. Input and output tokens are reported as mean±std across three repeated trials. Token counts are shown using K (thousands) and M (millions) for readability. Cached tokens are counted as regular input tokens for consistent accounting and comparison across settings.

Fig. 2: This gallery displays 24 representative benchmark cases from SciVisAgentBench, organized into four task suites: ParaView visualization, molecular visualization, bioimage visualization, and topology visualization. Each case shows the ground-truth visualization and its associated visualization operations.
